SSMA with linear correspondence constraints

Source: vignettes/ssma-linear-constraints.Rmd
ssma-linear-constraints.Rmd

SSMA aligns observations through domain-specific linear projections. Additional knowledge may concern features, groups of features, or averages of observations. linear_correspondence() represents these as weighted linear summaries of the projection coefficients. It works with unequal feature counts and partial links; no one-to-one correspondence between entire feature spaces is assumed. SSMA remains experimental: numerical agreement is not evidence of predictive benefit.

Objective and coordinate contract

For processed observations XsX_s, let Ys=XsWsY_s=X_sW_s. A correspondence adds

λ∑qdq∥(HsWs)q−(HtWt)q∥2\lambda\sum_q d_q\|(H_sW_s)_q-(H_tW_t)_q\|^2

to SSMA’s existing objective. It changes neither the observation graph nor its degree-based normalization. A single-domain linear_penalty() instead adds λ∑qdq∥(HsWs)q∥2\lambda\sum_q d_q\|(H_sW_s)_q\|^2, useful for smoothness or coefficient contrasts. These are soft, homogeneous quadratic penalties, not hard equalities.

Maps act on processed input features, before internal compression. They are never centered or standardized as observations. For arbitrary preprocessing, construct maps in its resulting feature coordinates explicitly; the package does not guess a raw-to-processed conversion. If Xprocessed=(X−μ)SX_{processed}=(X-\mu)S, a functional HH of raw coefficients becomes HSHS in processed coordinates. Intercepts are not part of this coefficient contract. Input-domain names and optional map row/column names are checked; unnamed map columns have positional semantics.

Matching feature summaries alongside observations

This generic example links summaries of two measurement systems with five and seven features. The maps could select homologous genes, average sensor groups, or describe linear calibration measurements.

x <- list(a = matrix(rnorm(24 * 5), 24, 5),
          b = matrix(rnorm(27 * 7), 27, 7))
h <- list(matrix(rnorm(4 * 5), 4, 5), matrix(rnorm(4 * 7), 4, 7))
link <- linear_correspondence(
  domains = c("a", "b"), maps = h,
  weights = c(1, 0, 2, 3), strength = 2, name = "measurements"
)
rows <- data.frame(domain_i = 1L, index_i = 1:12,
                   domain_j = 2L, index_j = 2:13)
fit <- ssma_align(
  x, correspondences = rows, constraints = list(link),
  preproc = NULL, ncomp = 3,
  control = ssma_align_control(knn = 8, sigma = 2, compression = "none")
)
fit$constraint_diagnostics

weights describe confidence in each matched summary. Zero confidence excludes a row. The default reduction="weighted_mean" normalizes confidence weights; "sum" preserves their magnitude. strength scales the resulting objective. Neither operation equalizes map units. Normalize measurement units deliberately, and choose strengths within the permitted training folds. Multiple objects have additive objectives. If a family spans many domain pairs, allocate its overall strength across those pairs explicitly; more pairs otherwise add more weight.

Rows with missing measurements should be omitted from the maps and weights, not filled with zeros. Named map rows must match in order. Feature names, when supplied on a map, must match the corresponding processed input in order.

Observation averages and smooth correspondences

Given averaging matrices AsA_s and AtA_t, use Hs=AsXsH_s=A_sX_s and Ht=AtXtH_t=A_tX_t. Rows can encode weighted windows, interpolation, or a declared temporal smoothing kernel. One-hot selectors recover ordinary sample-correspondence penalties when weights and reductions match. Helpers outside the alignment method should choose the windows and handle boundaries, missing samples, timing, and domain semantics.

Existing correspondences continue to support direct observation links. Set auto_correspondences=FALSE when the intended sample graph has no cross-domain links. This disables label/MNN discovery when explicit links are absent, which is particularly important when differently sized feature spaces have no common Euclidean coordinate system. Explicit links still apply.

Composition with PCA and covariance maps

With Zs=XsPsZ_s=X_sP_s, fit SSMA on ZsZ_s, supply maps HsPsH_sP_s, and recover original feature coefficients as Ws=PsBsW_s=P_sB_s. This is exact in the retained subspace; truncation discards information and can change the observation-neighbor graph. Preserve any scaling or whitening in the composed mapping.

For spatial or grouped-feature summaries GsG_s, GsPsG_sP_s constrains averages of projection coefficients. To constrain averages of covariance fingerprints Fs=CsPsBsF_s=C_sP_sB_s, instead supply GsCsPsG_sC_sP_s. For centered real observations this can be computed without a full feature-by-feature covariance matrix:

z <- x %*% p
h <- (g %*% t(x)) %*% z / (nrow(x) - 1)
fingerprint <- crossprod(x, z %*% b) / (nrow(x) - 1)

These are covariance fingerprints, not automatically standardized correlations or a guarantee that all feature-connectivity distances are preserved. Estimate covariances from actual observations, respecting nuisance processing, weights, missingness and validation folds. Projection weights and covariance patterns have different meanings.

compression="none" preserves already reduced features without allocating an identity basis. With the default internal SVD, the package projects maps through its basis and returns compression_bases; each NULL entry denotes identity. discarded_energy_fraction reports the unweighted Frobenius-energy fraction of each map outside the retained basis. It is a map-support diagnostic, not neural variance explained. Rank compression can remove useful constraints: inspect this quantity rather than assuming anatomical or low-variance directions survived.

Sparse maps, solvers, diagnostics and validation

Base matrices and numeric Matrix maps are accepted. Sparse maps remain sparse until reduced products require dense values. The operator solver applies maps and their transposes without assembling the global constraint matrix. The dense solver forms only reduced blocks. With compression disabled, the caller is responsible for choosing a manageable input dimension. This is not a streaming data loader.

Diagnostics report active row counts, reduction, strength, effective weight sum, per-component residuals, total residual and weighted objective contribution for each named constraint. Small residuals alone do not imply useful alignment: large strengths can suppress directions and contradictory constraints cannot generally all be satisfied. Inspect out-of-sample performance and appropriate shuffled-link controls separately.

The tests include independent outer-product and generalized-eigenproblem oracles, dense/operator agreement, sample-link equivalence, sparse and unequal feature spaces, null penalties, truncation, confidence splitting, contradictions, and permutation/rotation invariants. Fitted domains can be transformed using their own learned projections. This extension does not create a new-domain adaptation protocol; any use of an unlabeled target during fitting must be declared.
